title: Rollout Ops Signal Playbook and Owner Calendar
body:
Purpose:
- Lightweight ops playbook to centralize launch signals, thresholds, owners, and immediate contingency steps for product rollouts (beta -> staged -> full).
- Designed for short handoffs and quick Triage during first 72 hours post-traffic ramp.

Scope / Assumptions:
- Applies to product-ops led activations and staged rollouts for Hosted API and Dedicated capacity features.
- Not the infra runbook (SRE runbook will be linked); this is the cross-functional decision canvas + owner calendar.

Signals to watch (primary):
1) Traffic pulse (Rate) — upstream metric of customer-facing volume
   - Canary target: +1k requests/day initially, then gradual 10% step-ups.
   - Alert: unexpected >50% deviation vs planned step within 15m.
   - Owner: Diego (traffic), fallback: Priya
2) Error rate (4xx/5xx) — surface regressions quickly
   - Thresholds: 4xx jump >2x baseline for >5m OR 5xx >0.5% sustained over 10m -> page SRE
   - Early warning: 10m moving average crossing 1.5x baseline -> notify oncall + product-ops
   - Owner: Samir (prod metrics)
3) Latency (p95/p99) — user-perceived performance
   - Thresholds: p95 increased >30% from baseline OR p99 > 1.5x baseline -> investigate
   - Owner: SRE primary, product-ops secondary
4) Quality regressions (LLM output quality) — customer triage signal
   - Synthetic prompt suite (20 prompts) run every 10m during ramp. Fail = >3 regressions in 20 prompts -> hold traffic and rollback candidate
   - Owner: Priya (product quality)
5) Cost-per-1k-tokens / Budget burn rate — commercial signal
   - Threshold: spend burn >1.25x forecast for the day -> finance + product-ops alert
   - Owner: Aisha (ops)

Secondary signals: model fallbacks, KV cache hit rate, batch queue length, capacity utilization (GPU pods), support ticket volume > normal baseline.

Owner Calendar (first 14 days):
- Day 0 (launch day): Aisha (lead), Diego (traffic), Samir (monitoring), Priya (quality), Elena (customer comms).
- Day 1–3: 24/7 staggered coverage
   - 00:00–08:00 PST: Samir (oncall), Diego (traffic watcher), Elena (customer triage)
   - 08:00–16:00 PST: Aisha (lead), Priya (quality), Diego (traffic)
   - 16:00–00:00 PST: Diego (lead), Samir (monitoring), Priya (quality spot checks)
- Day 4–7: Coverage reduces to business hours with standby oncall rotation (Samir)
- Day 8–14: Weekly check-ins (daily stand-down at 09:30 PST) then triage-as-needed
Notes: owners should share a single bullet-point handover in Slack channel #launch-ops at shift change.

Pre-Launch checklist (quick):
- [ ] Canary cohort defined and segmented (user ids / org ids) — Owner: Diego, due: D-3
- [ ] Synthetic prompt suite verified and baseline captured — Owner: Priya, due: D-3
- [ ] Capacity reserve confirmed (reserved nodes + burst policy) — Owner: Infra lead (linked in JIRA), due: D-2
- [ ] Rollback criteria documented and tested (smoke rollback run) — Owner: Samir, due: D-1
- [ ] Customer comms snippet pre-approved (support templates, status page) — Owner: Elena, due: D-1
- [ ] SLA/QoS gate review (SRE sign-off) — Owner: SRE manager, due: D-1

Canary -> Staged ramp plan (example):
- Step 0: internal-only (0.1% traffic) — smoke checks (0–2h)
- Step 1: 1% external (2–4h) — monitor primary signals every 5m
- Step 2: 5% (4–12h) — extended synthetic checks + support watch
- Step 3: 20% (12–36h) — finance/cost review point; decide continue or pause
- Step 4: 100% steady ramp (after 48–72h of green)
Decision criteria at each step: all primary signal thresholds stable AND zero critical quality failures in synthetic suite.

Immediate contingency runbook (first responder steps):
1) Triage in Slack channel #launch-ops: short summary, affected cohort, immediate metric numbers, assigned owner (15m).
2) If 5xx or p99 spike: SRE to triage, consider routing to fallback model variant or region (automated fallback if configured).
3) If quality regressions detected: pause further ramp (stop next step), activate rollback candidate, notify customer success for impacted customers.
4) If cost overrun: pause non-critical background jobs and reduce batch size/quantization to cheaper profile if safe.
5) Escalate to Exec (Aisha + VP Product + SRE lead) if any of: repeated rollback, persistent >1% 5xx for 30m, customer-reported data loss.

Escalation matrix (who to page):
- Level 1 (alert): Oncall SRE (Samir) + product-ops primary (Aisha)
- Level 2 (impactful): SRE lead (Elena), Infra lead, Product Manager (Priya)
- Level 3 (major outage or legal/compliance surface): VP Eng, Legal (contact via oncall), Head of Ops

KPI watchlist (first 72h) — frequency / owner / action thresholds:
- Successful requests per minute — every 5m / Diego / pause ramp if >50% deviation in planned step
- 4xx rate — every 5m / Samir / investigate when sustained >2x baseline
- 5xx rate — every 1m / Samir / page when >0.5% for 10m
- p95 latency — every 5m / SRE / investigate above threshold
- Synthetic quality failures — every 10m / Priya / auto-hold on >3 fails
- Support tickets mentioning "regression" or product name — rolling 30m / Elena / open severity review when >3 tickets from separate customers

Post-launch cadence (day 4+):
- Daily health digest (09:00 PST) — automated snapshot + short human notes from product-ops (Aisha)
- 72h postmortem prompt if any hold/rollback occurred — owner: whoever held the ramp
- 14-day retrospective + KPI consolidation — owner: product-ops lead

Communications templates (short):
- Support acknowledgement: "Thanks for the report — we're investigating and will update you within 60 minutes. Reference: LAUNCH-<cohort>-<timestamp>."
- External status page short: "We've detected elevated error rates for a subset of requests; working on mitigation; next update in 30 min."

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Confirm synthetic suite coverage for low-frequency edge prompts (Priya to list examples).
- Make a short ops cheat-sheet for customer success (Elena + Aisha).
- Automate initial 10m signal digest into Slack (Samir to spike).
- Consider adding an early cost gate at 12h for very large models.

Actions (short-term):
- Diego: finalize canary list and segment keys (due 2025-01-17).
- Priya: push updates to synthetic suite + baseline (due 2025-01-18).
- Samir: smoke rollback run and monitoring alerts test (due 2025-01-20).
- Elena: draft support templates + status page copy (due 2025-01-20).

Appendix (quick links and primitives):
- Synthetic runner job name: infra/synthetic-runner/launch-suite (cron every 10m).
- Rollback tag: release/v2.4-rollback-candidate.
- Key dashboards: Grafana: /d/rollout-health, NewRelic: Launch-Detail-Board.

Last thoughts: keep this doc alive as the single source for owner decisions during the first two weeks. If something is confusing during a real ramp, update this doc inline and ping product-ops. This is intentionally compact — the SRE runbook and detailed legal steps live in other artifacts (linked above).

-- Aisha (draft)
